This file carries the **COST** and **PT** (provisioned throughput) family checks.\\n\\nSeverity scale: CRITICAL > HIGH > MEDIUM > LOW > INFO. Severity comes from each catalog row. A `workload-specific` threshold has no AWS-published value: name it as such next to the observed value, set it from observed usage, and keep the row\\'s severity.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 1. Cost methodology \u2014 billed first, token model second\\n\\nBedrock bills **four token types**, each at its own unit price: input, output, cache read, cache write. Unit prices also differ by **service tier** (Standard, Flex, Priority \u2014 where published) and by **routing** (in-region vs `cross-region-global`). Summing only input and output tokens at one rate per model is the most common cause of totals that do not match the bill. Sources: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/cost-mgmt-understanding-cur-data.html, https://aws.amazon.com/bedrock/pricing/\\n\\n**1a. Billed spend (Cost Explorer = billed truth).** Label these figures `(billed)`.\\n1. **Per model:** `aws ce get-cost-and-usage --group-by Type=PRODUCT_ATTRIBUTE,Key=model --metrics UnblendedCost UsageQuantity` (also `provider`, `inferenceType`, `feature`). Results come back keyed by display name (`model$Claude Sonnet 5`, `model$Nova Lite`); `model$` holds costs with no model. With `GroupBy`, each period\\'s `Total` is empty (`{}`): read the `Groups`, never take the empty `Total` as $0; a period with no `Groups` has no billed spend in that grouping. `Type=DIMENSION,Key=model` fails with `ValidationException`; product-attribute filters and `--dimension-key` are rejected by current CLI/SDK builds, so group rather than filter. Product-attribute data starts at a fixed date. A window that begins earlier fails with `DataUnavailableException`. Don\\'t assume the date: on that error, regroup the same window by `USAGE_TYPE` and say so. API: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-cost-management/latest/APIReference/API_GetCostAndUsage.html\\n2. **Per usage type** (any period): group by `USAGE_TYPE`. Lines encode model, token type, tier and routing, but naming varies \u2014 e.g. `USE1-NovaLite-input-tokens` vs `USE1-anthropic.claude-sonnet-5-mantle-input-tokens-standard` \u2014 so match a model\\'s lines loosely. `UsageQuantity` is often in thousands of tokens. {"id": "9836a570-f86d-4bce-8ad6-08f1504539fd", "role": "user", "content": [{"id": "tooluse_NG0tJBZxRDJjSl892gRy0Z", "content": "[{'text': '{\"content\": \"Find the log evidence that answers the investigative question, and check each candidate against a healthy baseline window before treating it as incident-related.\\\\n\\\\n## CloudWatch Logs\\\\n\\\\nQuery with `query_cloudwatch_logs` rather than `use_aws` (`start_query` with `get_query_results`, or `filter_log_events`). It runs one Logs Insights query against one log group and polls for about 30 seconds; a query still running after that returns an error, so narrow the time range or the filter and retry.\\\\n\\\\nA tool result larger than about 10K tokens (roughly 35K characters) is replaced by a short preview. Keep `limit` small (5 to 20) when you return raw records, and use `stats` or `pattern` to look at volume.\\\\n\\\\nLogs Insights details that are easy to get wrong:\\\\n- `sort` cannot take a function call such as `count()` or `bin(1m)`; alias it in `stats` and sort on the alias: `stats count() as n by bin(1m) as t | sort t`.\\\\n- Compare `@timestamp` with a number only inside `filter`; in `fields`, `stats` or `by` the comparison is a type mismatch.\\\\n- Convert times with the `datetime` tool rather than by hand; hand-computed Unix seconds can be a whole year off.\\\\n- A query whose window ends before a log group was created fails with \\\\\"end date is before the log group\\'s creation time\\\\\". `describe_log_groups` shows each group\\'s `creationTime`, so list an unfamiliar set of groups before querying it.\\\\n- `pattern @message | anomaly` groups messages into patterns and keeps only the statistically unusual ones, which makes it a cheap first look at a busy log group. `pattern` cannot be combined with `stats`.\\\\n- In a regex, `|` means OR, so `(error|500)` matches every \\\\\"500\\\\\" in timestamps and IDs. Match status codes in context, for example `status[:\\\\\\\\s]*\\\\\\\\b5\\\\\\\\d{2}\\\\\\\\b`.\\\\n- A `stats count() by bin(1m)` query over a range that spans the baseline and the incident compares a pattern\\'s frequency in one call.\\\\n\\\\nMore query patterns: [./references/query-examples.md](./references/query-examples.md).\\\\n\\\\n## Baseline and stopping\\\\n\\\\nA pattern that is about as frequent in a healthy window as in the incident window is pre-existing noise, not an incident signal. Find candidates in the incident window first, then check those patterns against the baseline.\\\\n\\\\nStop when the question is settled: a candidate has been validated against the baseline, or the window has been searched and shows nothing beyond baseline noise, in which case say what you searched.\\\\n\\\\nRecord each validated finding with `write_logs_observation`, with the query and time range in its analysis, unless your instructions have you state findings in your own reasoning instead.\\\\n\\\\n## Other log stores\\\\n\\\\n- S3-stored logs (CloudTrail, ELB access logs, VPC Flow Logs): [./references/s3-logs.md](./references/s3-logs.md)\", \"resource_manifest\": [\"references/azure.md\", \"references/datadog.md\", \"references/dynatrace.md\", \"references/grafana.md\", \"references/query-examples.md\", \"references/s3-logs.md\", \"references/splunk.md\"]}'}]", "status": "success", "type": "tool_result"}, {"id": "tooluse_tv8QagZ5PzAireIio1CBor", "content": "[{'text': '{\"123456789012\": {\"logGroups\": [{\"logGroupName\": \"/llmops-demo/bedrock-invocations\", \"creationTime\": 1792100924646, \"metricFilterCount\": 0, \"arn\": \"arn:aws:logs:us-east-1:123456789012:log-group:/llmops-demo/bedrock-invocations:*\", \"storedBytes\": 119011058, \"logGroupClass\": \"STANDARD\", \"logGroupArn\": \"arn:aws:logs:us-east-1:123456789012:log-group:/llmops-demo/bedrock-invocations\", \"deletionProtectionEnabled\": false, \"bearerTokenAuthenticationEnabled\": false}]}}'}]", "status": "success", "type": "tool_result"}], "created_at": null}

When it stops early it returns `continuation_timestamp`; pass that as the next `end_time` to page to older events.\\\\n- With no attribute, the tool returns only write events (`ReadOnly` is `false`), which is what a change timeline needs. Use an attribute to follow one resource, user or event name.\\\\n- Narrow before you page: exclude noisy event names and use windows of about 15 minutes. Excluded events do not count toward the size cap. `jmespath_filter` runs after the cap, so it shrinks the output but does not return more events.\\\\n- Passing `exclude_event_names` replaces the default exclusions (`CreateLogStream`, `Invoke`, `InvokeExecution`, `UpdateInstanceInformation`, `PutObject`); include them again if you still want them dropped.\\\\n- LookupEvents allows 2 requests per second per account and region, and one tool call may page several times, so run at most 2 CloudTrail calls at once.\\\\n- Start near the symptom onset and work backward until you find changes that address the question or have covered the requested timeframe.\\\\n\\\\nKubernetes events come from `use_kubectl`. RDS `describe_events` covers only the last 14 days; for an older window, use CloudTrail.\\\\n\\\\n## Judging a change\\\\n\\\\nA change during the incident window matters only if it relates to the investigative question or explains a symptom. When a change modified a resource that is now degraded, describe the resulting state, not just the event, and say whether that state deterministically stops the resource from working (an emptied security group, revoked IAM permissions, a black-hole route). {"id": "337f7c63-0c2d-41f5-b755-bd5818ca2aa0", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "# Bedrock output-token spend: findings for the last 30 days

**Bottom line:** I could not confirm "rising week over week with flat invocations". The data points the other way. The drift is a step-change that started on 2026-11-04, and it has been falling since the week of Nov 2.

- **Invocations:** they were not flat. Sonnet 5 went from about 100 calls/day to 1,000–2,000 on burst days.
- **Weekly output tokens:** the week of Nov 2 was the peak. The latest weeks are lower.
- **Billed Bedrock token spend:** it is $0.00 on every day from Oct 26 onward.

If the user's real bill is rising, it is probably in another account or Region, or it is the AgentCore Runtime line. The agent space has only one associated account, and I checked only that one.

## 2. Ranked drivers of Sonnet 5 output

Source is the Bedrock invocation log group (CloudWatch Logs Insights). The log group was created 2026-10-15, so it covers the whole window. Totals are 14,058 records and 18.07M output tokens from Oct 15 to Nov 20. These drivers overlap, so don't add them up.

1. **One prompt prefix, one family of jobs: 37.6% of output tokens.**
   - Prefix hash `3515ef73…` is 2,039 calls (14.5% of records) and 6.80M output tokens, averaging 3,334 output tokens per call.
   - Nov 4–5: IAM user `llmops-demo-admin`, `maxTokens` 4000. 979 calls, 3.13M output tokens. 380 calls (39%) stopped on `max_tokens`.
   - Nov 8, 9 and 17: role `user-c-AgenticAccess`, `maxTokens` 16000, no `max_tokens` stops, about 3.7–3.8k output per call.
   - Nov 10: role `user-e-session`, `maxTokens` 16000. 674 calls, 2.25M output tokens in one day.
   - This is a likely cause of the Nov 4, Nov 8 and Nov 10 spikes.
2. **Raised `maxTokens` = 16000: 26.6% of output.**
   - 1,663 end_turn calls produced 4.81M output tokens, averaging 2,895 per call. Most of this overlaps with driver 1.
   - The cap first appears in the logs on Nov 5 (6 calls), then 84 on Nov 7, 183 on Nov 8, 97 on Nov 9, 1,199 on Nov 10 and 94 on Nov 17.
   - Before Nov 4 the observed caps were 600–4000, and the largest single output in the 16k group is about 10.8k tokens.
3. **Tool-use agent loops with no `maxTokens` set: 34.5% of output.**
   - 7,326 `tool_use` calls produced 6.23M output tokens, about 851 per call. This is the steady, recent baseline.
   - It is concentrated in four AccountMgmt roles: user-d, user-a, user-b and user-f.
   - `user-a` alone accounts for essentially all Nov 16–20 volume: 1,089, 280, 230 and 222 calls per day.
   - Output per call is flat at 650–930 tokens. That means a high call count from agent loops or repeated tool calls, not longer outputs.
   - 53% of all Sonnet 5 requests (7,474 of 14,031) carry no `maxTokens` at all.
4. **`max_tokens` truncations.** 515 records (3.7% of records) produced about 1.95M output tokens (10.8%). 435 of them hit the 4000 cap.

## 3. Runaway or verbose output evidence

- **Raised cap, directly evidenced:** `maxTokens` 16000 appears from Nov 5, and driver 1 shows the matching spikes on Nov 8 and Nov 10.
- **Cap hits:** 380 of 979 calls on the Nov 4–5 job stopped on `max_tokens` at 4000. This is **LLM-COST-001 (MEDIUM)**, confirmed for that job only. Threshold is workload-specific. The AWS doc is `inference-parameters.html`.
- **No cap, directly evidenced:** the `tool_use` calls above have no `maxTokens`.
- **Not evidenced:** I found no reasoning or extended-thinking fields, and I did not check for them in the log payloads. I did not diff system prompts across days; I only hashed the first 2,000 characters. I found no tier shift: all usage types are `-standard` or `-global-standard`.
- **Model switch:** Opus 4.8 appeared on Oct 19–29 and Sonnet 5 on Oct 16 onward. Those dates are from the bill and logs, not from a CloudTrail change event.
- **Retries:** I did not check for retry storms. Call counts per day suggest loops, but that is inferred.

## 4. Prompt caching

- **Sonnet 5, no caching:** cache reads and writes are 0, measured in both CloudWatch and logs (14,031 records have the cache field present).
  - Repeated prefixes: top three hashes cover 2,567, 2,312 and 2,039 of 13,902 calls (18%, 17% and 15%).
  - Input floor: p10 is 1,847 tokens, p50 is 2,960, and average is 4,889.
  - Verdict: **LLM-COST-002 INFO (unconfirmed)**. I did not verify Sonnet 5's minimum cache-checkpoint size against the doc.
  - Effect on the question: caching only reduces input cost. It does not reduce output tokens.
- **GPT-5.6 Terra, caching in use but not paying off:** 4.99M cache-write tokens vs 0.57M cache-read tokens, a ratio of 8.8:1. This is **LLM-COST-002 (MEDIUM)**. It is billed at $0 (see section 5), so the dollar effect is not visible.
- **Opus 4.8:** cache reads exceed writes in the billed lines, for example 2.37M read vs 0.61M written in ap-south-1 on Oct 22. It looks healthy.

## 8. Savings opportunities (hypotheses, not billed figures)

All of these need pricing and a quality check before acting. Output tokens at the observed volumes:

1. **Cap `maxTokens` and add stop sequences on the driver-1 prefix.**
   - 16,000 → about 4,000–6,000 (tested value, not recommended).
   - Observed average is about 3.3k tokens per call.
   - The 4,000 cap truncated 39% of calls, so a cap must be set above the real p95.
2. **Set a `maxTokens` on tool-use loops.** Today none is set on 7,474 calls. Observed p95 output is about 1,100–1,800. Also review loop and retry counts in the `user-a` workload.
3. **Cheaper model for small calls (LLM-COST-004, MEDIUM, hypothesis).** 1,338 calls with caps of 600 and 1,200 average about 140–215 output tokens. Candidates are Haiku 4.5 or Nova Lite, after a quality evaluation.
4. **Batch or Flex (LLM-COST-003).** The Nov 4 and Nov 10 burst jobs look batch-able, but this is inferred, not evidenced. I did not check latency tolerance.
5. **Prompt caching on Sonnet 5** helps input cost only. It does not address the output-token question.
6. **Invocation log retention (LLM-COST-006, MEDIUM).** The log group has no retention set. It currently holds 119 MB. The fix is `aws logs put-retention-policy --log-group-name <log-group> --retention-in-days <N>`. N depends on the workload.
